review.alternative: Self-reference might be purely instrumental and avoidable through hierarchical separation of metalanguage.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that self-referential problem formulation can be proven free of paradox in open systems.

claims.statement: Self-reference and paradoxes present fundamental structural considerations when an agent evaluates its own goal space or formulates unassigned inquiries.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that self-referential reasoning structures are susceptible to foundational paradoxes.
support.passage: A major part of the philosophical interest in self-reference is centered around the paradoxes. A paradox is a seemingly sound piece of reasoning, based on apparently true assumptions, that still leads to a contradiction

review.alternative: Hidden degradation might be an artifact of specific prompt variations rather than a universal property of consensus.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that multi-agent consensus eliminates hidden degradation uniformly.

claims.statement: Aggregate performance improvements in collaborative verification systems can coexist with selective hidden-task degradation, complicating autonomous quality checks.

support.explanation: Highlights that apparent consensus or aggregate gains do not guarantee uniform reliability across all self-formulated or hidden tasks.
support.passage: Our experiments show that higher hidden-task accuracy can coexist with more counterexamples to non-degradation and lower non-degradation bounds.
